text: The model flagged this applicant as high‑risk because three key signals pushed the default probability up sharply. First, the record shows one instance of a serious delinquency— a payment that was 90 + days past due. That alone added a large amount to the risk score. Second, there are two recent 30‑to‑59‑day late payments, which further increased the model’s concern. Finally, the applicant’s revolving‑credit usage is very high—about 81 % of the available limit—showing that most of the credit line is already being used, which the model interprets as another strong warning sign. Together, these three factors drove the probability of default to 89.9 %, resulting in the “high risk” decision.
